new_statements.rule_in_words: Adioukrou is described (Hérault 1971) as a tone language with High, Mid, Low and a mostly-rising 'modulated' tone; the primary phonology makes no statement about word stress, and the LAPSyD coders therefore code stress as absent ('assumed none'). No first-hand statement locating word stress was found.
new_statements.domain_note: Database coding of the whole language from Hérault 1971; not a first-hand statement. Other opened sources (Hill 1995 fn.4: four tones H, L, falling, rising; Kaul 2006 summary: 2 tones; Hartell 1993: H/L/HL) speak only of tone and are silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to Adioukrou/Adjukru (adj, adio1239) as a whole; LAPSyD's entry is coded from Hérault 1971, whose data are from the Dabou-area variety. Glottolog's ref list for adio1239 also contains Abidji items (Werle 1971, Hager-M'Boua 2014, Vick 1990) which describe abid1235, not Adioukrou; the earlier scan's 'Werle 1971 phonology' is one of these.
